about.title: Wanderloom
about.quote: We are not a traditional travel agency. Every journey is built inside out: from reading the client’s personality, to engineering day one, to weaving the remaining days as chapters in one harmonious piece. The hotel is a note, the street a measure, the café a pause, the landmark a crescendo — all written in the keys of your taste, not off-the-shelf metrics.

aboutPage.description: We don't sell ready-made tickets and programs. We compose your trip like a single musical masterpiece: an intro, a verse, a climax, and a finale — entirely built around who you are, not what is sold to everyone.
aboutPage.sectionModelBody: Every client carries a different rhythm: calm or excitement, historical depth or visual wonder, street food or luxury experiences. We read this rhythm in your questionnaire, your conversation, your small details — then turn it into harmonious days where every stop serves the feeling you want to leave with.
aboutPage.sectionPhilosophyBody: A journey with us is not a list of landmarks, but a story. The hotel is chosen as a warm note or a loud interlude; walking the neighborhood is tuned to your energy; time between appointments is left on purpose so the scene can breathe. We believe luxury travel is when the plan disappears from view and only the experience remains.
aboutPage.sectionYouTitle: You are the center of the symphony
aboutPage.sectionYouBody: We do not impose a destination because it is famous — we build it because it fits your personality. Japan for lovers of fine detail differs from Japan for anime and cultural layers — and each is a project in itself.

japan.name: Japan
japan.desc: A stunning blend of ancient tradition and modern life — enchanting details at every turn.
insiderTips: Yanaka, Tokyo: a morning walk before museums open — local cafés absent from mass-tourism lists.
A Gion-side ryokan booked through our partner network — authentic omotenashi without an English-facing web presence.
Weekday local train to Kamakura: the Great Buddha and coastal forest without weekend crowds.
Nishiki Market, Kyoto after 9 p.m.: stalls officially closed, yet kitchen masters serve off-menu dishes for those who know the back alley.
